diagram_math_checks.justification: The Example at line 32 and supplier Statement define S={s1,...,s7} with both actions available at every state. Seven circles are the actual states; the rectangular any-current-state selector is explicitly not an eighth state. This encodes the same outgoing law for every s in S, including s7.

Supplier Statement says each of s1,...,s6 has conditional probability 1/6 under dashed; the six dashed arrows point from the selector to exactly those six circles. Their conditional probabilities sum to 6(1/6)=1. No dashed edge to s7 is drawn.

Example line 32 and supplier Statement specify probability 1 to s7 under solid. The sole solid arrow points from current-state selector to s7. Caption explicitly explains that setting the selector to s7 yields its solid self-transition. This prevents confusing lower-state behavior with an absorbing state under both actions.

Example line 32 specifies b(dashed|s)=6/7, b(solid|s)=1/7 and target always solid. Caption preserves these action probabilities separately from diagram conditional 1/6 and 1. Hence each upper behavior destination has (6/7)(1/6)=1/7 and lower has (1/7)(1)=1/7, agreeing with supplier proof step 1.1. Dashed edges are not target-policy transitions.

Upper label v_w(s_i)=2w_i+w8 for 1<=i<=6 and lower v_w(s7)=w7+2w8 exactly match Example line 32 and supplier phi(s_i)=2e_i+e8, phi(s7)=e7+2e8. Verification steps 1.1 and 2.1 remain unchanged and use explicit algebra, never the figure.
